changesProposed.name: Breakthrough Energy

verified.name: Breakthrough Energy
verified.thesis: Breakthrough Energy invests in businesses where the risk of failure is high and the timeframe for return on investment is 20 years. Clean technologies must be affordable and reliable to reach global scale. The firm invests across five sectors of the global economy to accelerate clean energy innovation.
verified.notes: Founded by Bill Gates at 2015 UN Climate Change Conference. Wikipedia identifies it as 'umbrella name of several organizations.' In March 2025, Bill Gates dissolved the Europe and US public policy units. Investment timeframe of 20 years contrasts with traditional VC 5-year horizon. AUM figures not provided in sources.

verified.name: Engine Ventures
verified.thesis: Engine Ventures invests in early-stage deep tech companies developing hardware-based technologies across biotech, robotics, green energy, agriculture, manufacturing, material science, and quantum computing.
verified.notes: Engine Ventures spun out as a separate investment firm from The Engine in 2023. The Engine itself is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit incubator and accelerator founded by MIT in 2016. Source [3] (Wikipedia) identifies this as 'Engine Ventures' but primarily describes The Engine organization. Source [4] is unrelated to Engine Ventures and was excluded from analysis. No current AUM, flagship fund name, or key partner names could be verified from provided sources.

changesProposed.name: Lux Capital

verified.name: Lux Capital
verified.thesis: Lux Capital invests in emerging science and technology ventures, focusing on early-stage technology companies in the areas of life sciences, defense, manufacturing, aerospace, and artificial intelligence. The firm backs companies that turn sci-fi into sci-fact.
verified.notes: Fund IX ($1.5B) closed in January 2026 as the firm's largest fund to date and was oversubscribed. Robert Paull is listed as co-founder on Wikipedia but not explicitly named as current partner on firm team page, so excluded from key_partners list.

changesProposed.name: Sequoia Capital

verified.name: Sequoia Capital
verified.thesis: Sequoia specializes in seed stage, early stage, and growth stage investments in private technology companies. The firm invests across clean tech, consumer internet, crypto, financial services, healthcare, mobile, and robotics sectors.
verified.notes: In November 2025, Alfred Lin and Pat Grady became joint managing partners succeeding Roelof Botha. Sequoia split into three independent entities in 2024: Sequoia (U.S./Europe), Peak XV Partners (India/Southeast Asia), and HongShan (China). In August 2025, COO Sumaiya Balbale resigned over handling of controversial statements by partner Shaun Maguire.

changes.current: Sequoia specializes in seed stage, early stage, and growth stage investments in private technology companies. The firm invests across clean tech, consumer internet, crypto, financial services, healthcare, mobile, and robotics sectors.
